Brunia Kolin, daughter of David, was born in 1911 in Zawiercie, Poland. In her childhood, she and her sister were orphaned of their parents, and the burden of supporting the family and raising her sister fell on Brunia. The hardships of her youth shaped her character, and at the same time they developed in her a sensitivity to injustice and a deep social awareness, which found expression in many conversations with her friends. She also read widely and attended theater performances.

In time she joined the youth movement Hashomer Hatzair and set her heart on emigrating to the Land of Israel and settling on a kibbutz. In 1931 she immigrated to Eretz Israel and joined Ein HaKoreh kibbutz, near Rishon LeZion. Even in the Land, suffering did not pass her by: in the first months of her stay on the kibbutz, she was accidentally wounded in the eye by a gunshot. She endured severe pain with courage.

When her sister, who had remained in Poland, was widowed and was left to care for three children, Brunia felt she was needed to support her. She was forced to leave the kibbutz and found work at the cooperative workers' restaurant in Tel Aviv. As in every job she had done, she excelled in her work at the restaurant as well and earned the appreciation of all her colleagues. After about a year of hard work, she felt very tired, and on 26 Av 5696 (14 August 1936) she went to rest at a convalescent home in the Carmel Forest. The car she was traveling in, accompanied by three Notrim, passed by the Arab village of Damun. At one of the bends in the road they encountered a barrier of stones, and from an ambush several volleys of fire were directed at the car. All the passengers in the car, including Brunia, were killed on the spot. She was laid to rest in the cemetery in Haifa.

Accounts of her life were published in the books *Bedam uBa'esh* (*In Blood and Fire*), *Me'orot Tarpa* (*The Events of 1936*), and in the collection *LeZecher Halalei Ya'arot HaCarmel* (*In Memory of the Fallen of the Carmel Forest*).
